title: Decoy: lure the piece, then check the line
outcomes: Finds a decoy sacrifice that mates or wins in an unlabeled set
Checks that the follow-up line is open
Rejects the sacrifice when the king has another square
Answers 'no tactic' when the lure leads nowhere

steps.text: In **Attacking the defender: remove, deflect, decoy, overload** the decoy was named for you. A decoy sacrifice lures a piece, often the king, onto a square where the next move punishes it. Before you sacrifice, ask two things: is the capture forced, and does the line your follow-up needs stay open? Solve this one, then follow the line.

line.say: The rook takes on f8 with check.

claims.statement: The engine's best move is among the accepted moves, and every accepted move is within 40 centipawns of it (depth 16).
Rxf8+ forces checkmate in 2 or fewer against the engine's best defence.
bxc4 is at least 6 pawns worse than the best move (depth 16).

steps.text: **A decoy holds when** the lured piece must take (a king in check often has no other move; other pieces can refuse) and the follow-up works on the new square. List every reply, not only the capture. A blocked line or one extra flight square turns the same sacrifice into a lost piece.

steps.title: Same sacrifice, one change each
steps.prompt: Predict first. In the first position, ...Rxf1+ lures the king. In the second, a white bishop stands on e4. In the third, the black knight stands on a8. Which still works?
In the positions where you rejected the sacrifice, what exactly did the opponent have that you had to find first: a flight square, a block, or a refusal?
